CFML Language Reference: Functions

CreateDateTime

Builds a complete date/time value from six numbers.

Category

Date and time functions

Syntax

CreateDateTime(year, month, day, hour, minute, second)

Parameters

year
Four-digit year, from 100 to 9999.
month
Month, 1 to 12.
day
Day of the month, 1 to the last day of that month.
hour
Hour, 0 to 23 (24-hour clock).
minute
Minute, 0 to 59.
second
Second, 0 to 59.

Returns

A date/time value, which prints as {ts '1999-12-31 23:59:59'}.

Usage

All six arguments are required. If any part is out of range (month 13, hour 24, June 31) the function throws an "Invalid date/time." error. Use DateFormat and TimeFormat together to display the result, and CreateODBCDateTime when you need the value inside SQL.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Midnight = CreateDateTime(1999, 12, 31, 23, 59, 59)>
<CFSET Rollover = DateAdd("s", 1, Midnight)>
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH></TH><TH>Raw value</TH><TH>Formatted</TH></TR>
<TR><TD>Last second of 1999</TD><TD>#Midnight#</TD>
    <TD>#DateFormat(Midnight, "mmm d, yyyy")# #TimeFormat(Midnight, "HH:mm:ss")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>One second later</TD><TD>#Rollover#</TD>
    <TD>#DateFormat(Rollover, "mmm d, yyyy")# #TimeFormat(Rollover, "HH:mm:ss")#</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
<P>Still running? Then your server is Y2K-ready.</P>
</CFOUTPUT>
